title: Guided tour of GamePlanIQ
intro: The tour walks through every part of the app, one screen at a time. Each stop explains what the screen is for and points at what to try. GamePlanIQ works on top of Little League Central Registration: register and pay there, import the roster here, run everything else in this app. Nothing you do during the tour can break anything; the demo can always be reset.
controls: Next moves to the following screen. Back returns to the previous one.
Skip this section jumps straight to the next part of the app.
Hide tucks the guide away so you can explore freely; Resume tour brings it back where you left off.
The tour signs you in as the right person for each part. You will notice the name in the top right change.

sections.title: Families
sections.summary: What a parent who never played baseball sees every day.

steps.title: A parent's home page
explain: You are signed in as the Parent: a mom or dad of two players who never played baseball.
Home shows only what matters today: field status, the next game or practice, anything the coach asked the family to do, and a report card waiting to be read.
The digest at the top says the same thing the daily email would say, so a family that never opens an app still knows what is happening.
try: Switch the digest from Today to Week to see the next seven days.

steps.title: The team page
explain: Every team has one page the whole team shares: roster, schedule, results, home practice, duties, carpools, photos and documents.
Only families on this team can see it. Phone numbers and addresses are never shown; messages go through the app.
try: Look along the tabs. Each one is a stop on this tour.

steps.title: Game-day duties
explain: Snacks, scorekeeper, dugout parent and pitch counter are listed per game.
A parent claims a slot with one tap and gets a reminder the day before. The coach sees who is covered and can nudge the whole team at once.
try: Open the Sign-ups tab, then tap I'll do it on an open slot.

steps.title: Carpools
explain: Any parent can offer seats to a game. Other parents add only their own child, and the driver is told who is riding.
This replaces the group text nobody can find on game morning.
try: Open the Carpool tab and tap Offer a ride on any game.

steps.title: Team photos
explain: Albums are visible to this team's families only.
A tagged player must have photo consent on file. If a family withdraws consent, their child's photos disappear from the album automatically.
try: Open the Photos tab.

steps.title: Schedule and the family calendar
explain: Games, practices, duties, registration deadlines and league events for every child in the family, in one place.
Family calendar builds one file the phone's calendar app can subscribe to, with reminders already set.
try: Tap Family calendar and look at what is included.

steps.title: The end-of-season tournament
explain: Families follow the bracket from the schedule page. Every game is on the team calendar, and when a coach taps Final in the scorebook the winner moves on by itself.
No one has to update a whiteboard at the snack stand.
try: Find the Comets in the bracket and see who they play next.

steps.title: A player's report card
explain: The head coach rated ten skills, celebrated three strengths and picked one thing to work on for the Player, age nine.
The app chose the lessons that teach that one thing, written for his age.
Report cards are private to the family, the coach and the league office. They are never a ranking and never shared between families.
try: Tap Mark as read so the coach knows the family saw it.

steps.title: A lesson for a scared kid
explain: Every lesson is written for the parent who never played: what to do, what to say, what to avoid, a verified drill video, and a ten-minute backyard practice.
Marking a lesson done feeds the player's progress and badges.
try: Open the Parent coaching tab to see what to say and what to avoid.
Mark done at the bottom records the lesson for the player.

steps.title: Parent Academy
explain: Guides for the questions parents actually ask: what equipment to buy, how to handle a bad game, what the rules of the division are, how pitch counts work.
Content is organised by the child's age, so nothing here is over a family's head.
try: Open any guide that catches your eye, then press Next.

steps.title: Build a backyard practice
explain: Pick a skill and the minutes available. The generator builds a warm-up, two or three drills and a fun challenge sized to the child's age.
The plan can be run from a phone with a timer, or printed.
try: Tap Generate my practice.

steps.title: Messages
explain: Team threads and direct messages with the coach, with no phone numbers exchanged.
Player accounts cannot send messages at all; adults on a team can only reach that team's families.
try: Open the team families thread.

steps.title: Notification Center
explain: Every notice the family received: game changes, duty reminders, report cards, carpool updates.
Each person chooses which topics they want and quiet hours. Urgent notices such as a rainout always get through.
try: Tap a notification to jump to the thing it is about.

steps.title: Account and privacy
explain: Children, consents and contact preferences live here. Photo consent and video review consent can be changed at any time and take effect everywhere immediately.
Families can download everything the league holds about them.
try: Look at the consent switches for each child.

steps.title: Forms the league needs
explain: Medical information, consents and anything else the league asks for are forms, built by the league office from templates. Parents fill them in once per child from a phone.
Medical answers are seen only by the child's coaches, the safety officer and the president.
try: Pick the Player, answer the required questions, and tap Submit.

steps.title: A player's whole history
explain: One timeline for the Player across seasons: teams, positions played from the lineup cards, attendance, tryout scores, report cards, badges, pitch counts and coach evaluations.
This follows the player from T-ball to Majors so next year's coach starts with the full picture.
try: Scroll to History and filter by Report card or Game.

steps.title: Registration
explain: Registering a child takes five steps on a phone: child, division, forms, payment, review.
Eligibility and age are checked as you go, so the league office never has to send a form back. Families can pay in three monthly installments; the schedule and reminders are set up automatically.
Most Little Leagues register through Little League Central Registration; in that case this step happens there and the roster is imported.
try: Walk the first step or two. You can stop anywhere.

sections.title: Players
sections.summary: What a nine-year-old sees on his own account.

steps.title: A player's own account
explain: You are now in the Player's own account. He is nine, so the account is managed by his parent: the name at the top right stays Parent, the role changes to Player, and every screen is his.
There are no messages, no leaderboards and no comparison to teammates. He sees his next game, his coach's home practice, his badges and a quick Baseball IQ question.
try: Notice what is missing compared with his dad's home page.

steps.title: Baseball IQ
explain: Situational questions on a diamond: tap where the ball should go. Some answers are acceptable rather than right or wrong, and each one is explained in kid language.
Fifty questions and fifteen short lessons, all written for children.
try: Answer two questions and read the explanation.

steps.title: Challenges and badges
explain: Lessons done, practices completed and quizzes passed earn badges. Challenges are set by the league and are about effort, never about statistics.
try: Open a badge to see how it was earned.

sections.title: Coaches
sections.summary: Everything a volunteer coach needs, on one page and on a phone.

steps.title: Coaches' Headquarters
explain: You are the Head Coach of the Minor Comets: a volunteer parent with one season of coaching behind him.
One page holds his teams, practice planner, game day, certification progress, tryout scoring and All-Star ballots.
try: Look at the certification progress and the tryout card.

steps.title: Team tools
explain: Roster with notes and skills, attendance, home practice assignments, report cards, lineups and game-day duties.
Assigning a home practice sends every family the same lesson and shows the coach who completed it.
try: Open the Report cards tab to see the drafts in progress.

steps.title: Season curriculum
explain: The head coach assigned the league's intermediate program to the Comets. The card shows this week's focus and lessons, and colours every week by whether it was actually run.
A week counts when a completed practice or a home assignment that week teaches one of its lessons. The board sees the same thing for every team, to know where to offer help.
try: Hover a week to see which practice covered it.

steps.title: Player evaluations
explain: A coach evaluation form, one per rostered player, built by the league office. The head coach has done six of his twelve Comets.
Answers feed each player's history and next season's team formation. Families never see other players' evaluations.
try: Pick a player without a tick, rate effort, and tap Submit.

steps.title: Game day: the lineup card
explain: The lineup card checks the league's minimum-play rule, bench innings and pitcher rest before first pitch.
Warnings advise; they never block the coach.
try: Tap Game day, then Auto-rotate the rest.

steps.title: Practice planner
explain: Choose the focus and the time. The planner builds a practice from the drill library with stations, cues and the drill video for each block.
try: Build a plan, then open it.

steps.title: Run a practice from a phone
explain: A plan becomes a full-screen timer with coaching cues, the drill's setup diagram and the video one tap away. Attendance is taken on the same screen.
Finish logs the practice, counts it toward the season curriculum, and sends the home assignment.
try: Tap Run practice, then Start. Use the Back arrow in the tour when you are done.

steps.title: Pitch counts and rest days
explain: Pitch counts from the scorebook become required rest days automatically, by age. A pitcher who is resting is flagged on the lineup card.
try: Find a pitcher who is resting.

steps.title: Tryout scoring
explain: Six stations, scored one to five on any phone. Every evaluator's scores roll into the draft board the commissioner runs.
try: Score a player with Save and next, then open Rankings.

steps.title: Coach certification
explain: Six safety and conduct modules with a short check at the end of each. The league sees who is ready to be around players; nobody chases paper.
try: Open the heat and lightning module.

steps.title: All-Star ballots
explain: Coaches nominate and vote. The tally is private until the commissioner finalises it, and only selected families are told.
try: Look at the nominees and the ballots received.

sections.title: League office
sections.summary: What the president and board run the league with.

steps.title: The dashboard
explain: You are the League President.
The attention list comes first: documents to review, schedule conflicts, a live draft, coaches not yet certified, fields needing a call.
try: Scroll the attention list, then look at Field status.

steps.title: Registration
explain: Every submitted registration with its documents, payment and eligibility check. Approve, waitlist or ask for a correction in one place.
try: Open a submitted registration.

steps.title: Teams and rosters
explain: Teams by division with coaches, roster counts and logos. Moving a player between teams updates every family's schedule and calendar.
Divisions that do not draft use Form teams: siblings stay together, buddy and coach requests from registration are honoured, and groups are dealt out so size and strength stay even.
try: Choose the Coach pitch division, then tap Form teams to preview balanced teams.

steps.title: Players, guardians and CSV import
explain: Every player and guardian account in the league.

Import CSV brings the roster over from Little League Central Registration: pick Sports Connect or PlayMetrics as the source, paste the export, and every row is checked and previewed before anything is written.
try: Tap Import CSV, choose PlayMetrics as the source, and use the example row.

steps.title: Tryouts, draft and All-Stars
explain: Tryout scores become a snake draft with balance warnings that advise, never block.
All-Star nominations, ballots and the tally live here too.
try: Open the Drafts tab, open the Minor draft board, then tap Pick best available.

steps.title: Scheduling
explain: Drag a game to another day. Field, team, shared-coach and umpire conflicts are flagged as you go.
The rainout tool closes a field, moves or cancels its games and tells every family in one step.
try: Open the Rainout tool, then cancel.

steps.title: Fields and weather
explain: Field status is what every family sees on their home page. Changing it here changes it everywhere at once.
try: Set a field to open or closed.

steps.title: Volunteers and certification
explain: Shifts, background checks and coach certification in one place, with reminders sent through the notification rules.
try: Open the Coach certification tab.

steps.title: Safety
explain: Incident reports with safety-officer review, a safety plan builder with starter text for every required section, and first-aid kit checks per field.
try: Open an incident or the safety plan.

steps.title: Umpires
explain: Assign umpires with availability, conflict and weekly-load hints. Pay rates per division, a pay tally and recorded payments.
try: Assign an umpire to an unassigned game.

steps.title: Finances and budget
explain: Registration revenue, expenses, financial assistance and budget versus actual by category.
Payment plans split a balance into monthly installments; overdue and due-this-week reminders go out through the notification rules. Card processing connects at deployment.
try: Open the Payment plans tab and record an installment.

steps.title: Field improvement calculator
explain: A board-ready estimate for turf and field projects: cost ranges, maintenance savings and a printable summary.
try: Change a field size and watch the totals.

steps.title: Sponsors and fundraising
explain: Sponsors with logos, levels and what they were promised. Sponsor logos appear on the public site and the team pages.
try: Open a sponsor.

steps.title: The public website
explain: Change the headline, banner, documents and board page, then publish. No rosters or player names are ever public.
try: Edit the headline, Publish changes, then View public site.

steps.title: Communications and notification rules
explain: One announcement reaches the right audience.
Every notification follows published rules: who is told, which topic switch it honours, and whether it waits for morning.
try: Scroll to Notification rules.

steps.title: Academy content
explain: Lessons, videos, Baseball IQ questions and curricula can be adjusted per league, with version history and revert to the platform original.

The Diagrams tab draws a drill: players, cones, equipment and throw or run arrows that appear on the lesson page and in the practice runner. The Curricula tab shows which teams follow their program week by week.
try: Open the Diagrams tab and tap Draw diagram on any drill.

steps.title: Staff and permissions
explain: Board members, commissioners, coaches and officers with exactly the permissions their role carries. Every action in the app is checked against these, not just hidden in menus.
try: Open a role to see its permissions.

steps.title: Forms and evaluations
explain: Build any form the league needs from a template or from scratch: coach evaluations per player, medical information, volunteer applications, coach feedback, field requests.
Each purpose decides who may read the answers. Reminders and completion counts are built in.
try: Open Results on the mid-season evaluation.

steps.title: Tournaments
explain: End-of-season tournaments, All-Star brackets and jamborees: round robin, single or double elimination, or pools followed by a bracket.
Games go on the schedule like any other, and a final from the scorebook advances the bracket on its own.
try: Open the Minor Championship bracket and score a ready game.

steps.title: Surveys
explain: Season surveys from templates. Results are anonymous to the board, broken down by division and compared with last year.
try: Open the results of the parent survey.

steps.title: Reports
explain: Numbers for the board meeting: rostered players, academy participation, home practices, volunteer coverage, registrations by division and the audit log, each exportable as CSV.
try: Export any report.

steps.title: Season close-out
explain: A checklist for the end of the season: awards with an engraving export, uniform returns, equipment inventory, banquet, and the archive.
try: Tick a task on the checklist.

steps.title: Seasons and settings
explain: Seasons, divisions and play rules, eligibility, pitch counts, registration, quiet hours and branding.
Roll over on the Seasons tab creates next season with divisions and fields carried forward. The Branding tab holds the read-only board overview link for sponsors and officials.
try: Open the Divisions tab and look at the play rules for a division.

sections.title: Platform
sections.summary: How a new league is set up in fifteen minutes.

steps.title: Super administrator
explain: You are now the platform administrator, who looks after every league on GamePlanIQ.
Leagues, subscriptions, platform content and system health across every tenant.
try: Look at the league list.

steps.title: Onboard a league
explain: Name, colours, season, divisions, teams and fields. The wizard ends on a working league office ready for the CSV import you saw earlier.
try: Tap Onboard a league and walk the steps. Create league at the end makes a real demo league you can explore.

steps.title: The league's public website
explain: Built from the content the league office edits: schedule, fields, registration, documents, sponsors and board contacts.
No rosters, no player names, no photos without consent. Registration from here leads straight into the app.
try: Scroll the page, then press Next to finish.

closing.title: That is the whole app
lines: Everything you saw runs on one shared database with role-based permissions checked on every action.
Little League Central Registration stays the system of record for registration and fees; GamePlanIQ imports the roster and runs everything else.
Payments, email and text messages connect at deployment; the in-app record and the family calendar work today.
Restart the tour any time from the menu, or reset the demo data to start fresh.
